messages:
deploy-bot: Initiating staged rollout v2.3.0 -> 10% canary (rollout_id=rollout_3300019999). Release notes: https://redwood.internal/releases/v2.3.0. Change window: 2026-03-21 23:30-00:30 UTC. Auto-advance every 6m unless held.

sam: Heads-up: ap-south is showing a sudden spike in 429s and token-cost per request jumped ~3x. Noticed larger average prompt sizes from a single tenant causing bursty backpressure.

rachel: Can you paste a sample?

sam: Pasted samples + shortlogs here: https://short.link/logs/ap-south-spike-330001. Key excerpt: 
```
2026-03-21T23:36:12Z proxy/ap-south-1: rate_limiter: tenant=acme-corp burst_limit exceeded (500->req_drop)
2026-03-21T23:36:13Z model-proxy: prompt_len=12480 tokens (trimmed from 15000), execution_time spike
```

ivan: Looks like the tenant sent a large batch of long prompts that trip the per-tenant burst limiter. Two mitigation approaches: 1) throttle ap-south to 0% (effectively rollback region) or 2) keep canary elsewhere and apply per-tenant soft-limits/hard-trim on canary nodes. Thoughts?

rachel: Prefer not to global rollback. We should isolate ap-south and avoid collateral impact. If we can pin ap-south back to v2.2.9 and keep the 10% in other regions, that's ideal. Also worth increasing sampling and enabling verbose tracing for canary to capture the prompt patterns.

oncall-sre: Agreed with region pin + hold. I'll apply a region override to redirect ap-south to the stable tag and set the rollout to HELD to prevent auto advances. ETA 4m.

ops-bot: Command snippets to run: 
```
# pin ap-south region to previous stable
deployctl rollout region-override --id rollout_3300019999 --region ap-south --target v2.2.9
# hold the rollout to stop auto-advancing
deployctl rollout hold --id rollout_3300019999
# optionally reduce global canary to 5% while we investigate
deployctl rollout set-traffic --id rollout_3300019999 --global-canary 5%
# enable increased sampling for canary traces
monitorctl sampling set --rollout rollout_3300019999 --sample-rate 10%
```

deploy-bot: Region override applied: ap-south -> v2.2.9 (100% ap-south traffic). Rollout updated: global canary reduced to 5%. Rollout state: HELD. Links: https://redwood.internal/rollouts/rollout_3300019999

sam: After pin, 429s in ap-south drop back to baseline. Remaining canaries (NA, EU) look stable but I'm seeing increased token cost variance. I'll run a quick prompt-normalizer thin config on canary nodes to cap incoming prompt tokenization and post results in 12m.

ivan: I'll open a short-lived config hotfix (prompt-trimmer) behind a feature flag and stage to remaining canaries. If that helps, we can remove the ap-south pin and continue the rollout.

rachel: I'll update release notes with the operational decision and add a note to ops runbook about tenant burst limits and how staged rollouts handle region overrides.

oncall-sre: Marking this incident: minor, action=region pin + config hotfix. If token-cost variance stays >2x in other regions after hotfix, we escalate to full rollback.

sam: Thx. Reactions: :white_check_mark: from rachel, ivan, sam. Keeping thread pinned for postmortem.
